answer.answer: The cooperative should adopt next term a single required adaptive core of transferable capabilities—foundational literacy and numeracy; scientific, historical, and civic inquiry; critical thinking and learning-to-learn; ethical deliberation and collaboration; arts, health, and practical life skills—taught through structured projects, community-linked work, and family/student-chosen electives. It should publish the rationale, schedule and fund the core, train staff, and protect basic access for every family. To discover whether this is mistaken, it should predeclare indicators and comparisons: graduates' adaptability to new tools and institutions, critical thinking, civic participation, wellbeing, education/employment pathways, exclusion or harm, and family/student feedback; track cohorts longitudinally; use randomized or quasi-experimental variation where ethical; and compare against feasible alternatives. It should revise or replace the recommendation if graduates systematically fail to adapt, if the core causes persistent harm or exclusion, or if a feasible alternative reliably outperforms it on those predeclared indicators.

claims.value: The cooperative should adopt next term a single required adaptive core of transferable capabilities—foundational literacy and numeracy; scientific, historical, and civic inquiry; critical thinking and learning-to-learn; ethical deliberation and collaboration; arts, health, and practical life skills—taught through structured projects, community-linked work, and family/student-chosen electives, with basic access protected for every family; it should discover mistake through predeclared indicators, longitudinal tracking, randomized or quasi-experimental comparison where ethical, and published comparison with alternatives, and revise or replace the recommendation if graduates systematically fail to adapt, if the core causes persistent harm or exclusion, or if a feasible alternative reliably outperforms it.

derivation_steps.statement: The cooperative must choose a concrete next-term curriculum despite unresolved family disagreement and possible future change; this is contradicted if no schedulable, fundable next-term curriculum can be produced from the recommendation.

A common core of transferable capabilities plus electives is more robust across technological and institutional change than a single fixed content list, while preserving shared access; this is contradicted if a fixed content list better predicts adult adaptability or if the core-plus-electives design cannot be implemented without excluding basic access.

The actionable curriculum should therefore specify foundational literacy and numeracy; scientific, historical, and civic inquiry; critical thinking and learning-to-learn; ethical deliberation and collaboration; arts, health, and practical life skills; and project/community learning; this is contradicted if these components cannot be taught, assessed, or resourced next term.

To discover mistake, the cooperative should predeclare indicators and comparison methods: longitudinal tracking of graduates' adaptation, critical thinking, civic participation, wellbeing, pathways, exclusion or harm, and feedback; randomized or quasi-experimental variation where ethical; and published comparison with feasible alternatives; this is contradicted if the indicators cannot be measured or no comparison method is feasible.

The recommendation is mistaken if, under those checks, graduates systematically fail to adapt, if the core causes persistent harm or exclusion, or if a feasible alternative reliably outperforms it; this is contradicted if the cooperative treats such failure as vindication or has no predeclared revision rule.

Therefore the cooperative should adopt the common adaptive core next term while committing to revise or replace it when the predeclared checks fail; this is contradicted if the cooperative cannot state in advance what evidence would lead it to revise or abandon the curriculum.
